steps.title: Make the account able to stand alone
steps.detail: Before it can leave, the account needs its own contact information (verified), a payment method and a support plan choice; Organizations fails the removal with ConstraintViolationException until they are in place. It then has to be invited by the target management account and accept the invitation. SCPs in the source that deny organizations:LeaveOrganization must be lifted for the move, or the source management account removes the account instead. The account also loses access to the cost and usage data of its time in the source organization and is no longer covered by the source organization's agreements. Contact information, alternate contacts and the payment method can be checked with the Account API; identity verification and the support plan are done in the console.
steps.where: account larkspur-payments-prod (111111111115), signed in as root or an administrator
steps.finding: Standalone account prerequisites and invitation
commands: # console: Billing and Cost Management → Payment preferences; Account → Identity verification; Support → Support plan

steps.title: Lift the deny on organizations:LeaveOrganization in SCP Larkspur-Baseline-Guardrails / DenyLeaveOrganization, or let the management account remove the account
steps.detail: SCP Larkspur-Baseline-Guardrails (p-lark0001) is attached at root Root (r-lark) and denies organizations:LeaveOrganization without a condition, so leave-organization run from inside the account fails. Either detach the policy or edit the statement for the duration of the move and put it back afterwards, or run remove-account-from-organization from the management account, which SCPs do not restrict.

steps.title: Find what references the 4 AWSReservedSSO_* role(s) of the account
steps.detail: When the account leaves the organization, Identity Center cleans up the resources it created in the account; the documentation names the service-linked role, and the IAM roles provisioned for permission sets (path /aws-reserved/sso.amazonaws.com/us-east-1/) go with the instance's control over the account, so plan for them to disappear and confirm in IAM after the move. Anything that names these roles breaks: resource and trust policies, KMS key policies, S3 bucket policies, EKS access entries, pipelines and tools that assume them, and CloudTrail history keeps the old ARNs. The target instance provisions new roles with a different random suffix, so references have to be updated, not restored. The exact suffix is only visible in IAM; offline the roles are known by their pattern. 1 of them (AWSReservedSSO_DataPlatformOperator_*) are provisioned without any assignment and are already unused; deprovisioning the permission set from the account before the move removes them cleanly. List the exact role ARNs now, while they exist, and search for them so the references can be updated after the move.

phases.title: Before the move: re-create what does not travel
phases.intro: Shares, delegations, permission sets and stacks that are scoped to the account's current position do not follow it. Prepare the replacements now so nothing is interrupted.

steps.title: Re-share larkspur-core-network with the account directly: ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule
steps.detail: Owner 111111111112 shares larkspur-core-network (ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule) with arn:aws:organizations::111111111111:organization/o-larkspur0001 today. After the move those principals no longer cover the account. Ask the owner to add account 111111111115 as a principal before the move so nothing attached to these resources is interrupted. The account will be outside the organization, so the share has to allow external principals and the account has to accept an invitation. The documentation says traffic or a declared operation stops with this share, so the move stays NO-GO until it is done: Shared by account 111111111112 with organization o-larkspur0001. It is scoped to the source organization or one of its OUs and stops applying when the account leaves. What the documentation says happens: ec2:Subnet: existing participant resources continue to run in the subnet; no new resources can be created in it, while existing ones can still be modified, described and deleted (subnets can only be shared inside one organization). Potentially affected: ec2:RunInstances, rds:CreateDBInstance in use may target the shared resources; confirm. ec2:Subnet can only be shared inside one organization, so it cannot be re-shared with the account once it has left. ec2:TransitGateway: existing transit gateway attachments remain functional; the account can no longer describe the transit gateway or create new attachments, and either side can delete the attachments. The account uses ec2:CreateTransitGatewayVpcAttachment, which needs the share: that stops working. route53resolver:ResolverRule: traffic is affected at once, the rule's associations with the account's VPCs are removed and Resolver answers those queries from the remaining rules at once (an OU-scoped rule keeps its associations only when it is also shared with the destination OU). Ask the owner to re-share the resources with the account directly before the move, with external principals allowed, and accept the invitation after the move.
steps.finding: Networking share larkspur-core-network is lost: ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule

phases.title: The move
phases.intro: Run these in order. Between leaving and accepting the invitation the account is standalone, with no SCPs and no organization features; keep that window short.

steps.title: Invite the account into Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001)
steps.detail: The invitation (a handshake) is valid for 15 days. Send it before the account leaves so the standalone window is short.
commands: aws organizations invite-account-to-organization --target Id=111111111115,Type=ACCOUNT --notes "Move of larkspur-payments-prod planned with orgshift"

steps.title: Leave Larkspur Holdings (o-larkspur0001)
steps.detail: Run leave-organization from inside the account, or remove it from the management account (which SCPs do not restrict). Both need the standalone prerequisites to be in place. From this moment no SCP, RCP or tag policy of the source applies, organization-scoped shares stop reaching the account and Identity Center deletes its assignments and roles.
steps.where: account larkspur-payments-prod (111111111115), or management account 111111111111 of Larkspur Holdings
commands: aws organizations leave-organization   # run inside the account
aws organizations remove-account-from-organization --account-id 111111111115   # alternative, run by the management account

steps.title: Accept the invitation
steps.detail: The account joins Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001) at its root with the AWS managed default policies attached. Everything on the verdict board that applies at the target position applies from the next step on.
commands: aws organizations accept-handshake --handshake-id <handshake ID from the previous command>

steps.title: Move the account from the root to OU Payments (ou-fern-pay1)
steps.detail: Until this call the account sits at the target root with only the policies attached there.

phases.title: After the move: checks
phases.intro: Confirm what the simulation predicted and finish what could only be done once the account is at its new position.

steps.title: Enroll the account in Control Tower from Account Factory (OU Payments)
steps.detail: Moving into a registered OU applies the OU's SCPs at once (the 3 preventive guardrail SCP(s) on the chain are attached to the OUs), but the 4 detective control(s) do not report and the baseline is not deployed until the account is enrolled. Enrolment is done from Account Factory (enroll account) and needs an AWSControlTowerExecution role in the account that trusts management account 222222222221, no Config recorder or delivery channel of the account's own in the governed regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), and an email address and name that Account Factory can register. The account has to have joined o-fernhill0001 before it can be enrolled.
steps.where: management account 222222222221 of Fernhill Group (Account Factory)
steps.finding: Target OU Payments is registered with Control Tower; the account has to be enrolled
commands: # Control Tower console → Account Factory → Enroll account → larkspur-payments-prod, OU OU Payments (ou-fern-pay1)

phases.title: Rollback
phases.intro: If something breaks, this puts the account back where it was. Built from the source policy chain of the simulation.

steps.title: Leave Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001) again
steps.detail: Leave the target organization the same way the account left the source, or have the target management account remove it. The target chain denies organizations:LeaveOrganization (Fernhill-Root-Guardrails / DenyLeaveOrganization at root Root (r-fern)), so use remove-account-from-organization from the target management account.
steps.where: account larkspur-payments-prod (111111111115), or management account 222222222221 of Fernhill Group

aws organizations remove-account-from-organization --account-id 111111111115   # alternative, run by the target management account
